en: The Dyad of the Dissociated from the Fettered and the Fetterable (Ganthavippayutta-Ganthaniya-Duka)
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the ties and not conducive to the ties, a state that is dissociated from the ties and not conducive to the ties arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the ties and not conducive to the ties, a state that is dissociated from the ties but not non-conducive to the ties arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the ties and not conducive to the ties...
Dependent on [a state] dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties, states that are dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties, a state dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on states that are dissociated from the ties (*ganthavippayutta*) and not subject to the ties (*na-ganthaniya*), as well as states that are dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties, there arises a state that is dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five;
under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are five. (The full detail applies everywhere.
The Chapter on the Ties (*Ganthagocchaka*) is finished.
